📚 Today you learned

The Russell 2000 — Your Discovery Hunting Ground's Benchmark

The Russell 2000 tracks the 2,000 smallest stocks in the Russell 3000 (roughly $300M-$5B market cap) — the small-cap index, versus the S&P 500's large-cap focus. It gained +0.94% Friday on the soft jobs print, which matters more to you than it does to a GOOG/SPXC-only portfolio: this is the universe stock-finder actually hunts in (breakouts, volume surges, momentum) when it scans for your next 5-15% trade, not mega-caps. When Russell 2000 is outperforming the S&P — small caps leading — that's a risk-on tape where momentum setups tend to work better and get more follow-through. When it's lagging or rolling over, the same breakout patterns fail more often; it's chop, not trend. Check IWM (the Russell 2000 ETF) relative to SPY before leaning hard into a stock-finder pick — it's a quick read on whether the tape favors what you're about to trade.

Also today: Small-cap liquidity premium — small caps trade at a valuation discount partly because they're harder to exit in size; irrelevant at your position sizes, but it's why institutions can't just buy the index and are often absent from names stock-finder surfaces — less competition for you.
